name: New Market Trading
rootCause: The New Market Trading "SquidRouterModule" is a Gnosis Safe module built on Axelar's AxelarExpressExecutableWithToken. The Axelar express fast-path (expressExecuteWithToken) is permissionless by design (any relayer may front tokens) and performs NO gateway/cryptographic validation of the message. The module's _executeWithToken override only checks that a caller-SUPPLIED sourceAddress string equals the public squidRouter address — a value the caller fully controls — and never validates the real caller or a genuine Axelar gateway proof. _processPayload then decodes the target safe and delegate directly from the attacker-supplied payload and executes actions against the Safe, checking only that delegate holds permission (never msg.sender == delegate). The attacker called expressExecuteWithToken with amount = 0 (fronting nothing), the public squidRouter address string, and a forged payload naming the victim Safe, a real public NMT delegate that already held APPROVE+SWAP permission, and three actions (ERC20 approve -> Permit2 approve -> Uni V3 swap exact-in) that swap the Safe's entire USDC into a worthless attacker-controlled "u" token via the whitelisted Universal Router. This drained ~88 Safes (~$3.98M total). Root cause: missing caller/gateway authentication on the express path plus trusting payload-supplied delegate/safe. descriptions.text: SquidRouterModule Missing Caller Check. Lost: ~$3.98M USD

$3.98 million drained from 88 Gnosis Safes across three chains on New Market Trading. A third-party Safe module trusted caller-supplied data over msg.sender. One missing require check. Anyone who read the source code could drain every wallet.

The New Market Trading "SquidRouterModule" is a Gnosis Safe module built on Axelar's AxelarExpressExecutableWithToken. The Axelar express fast-path (expressExecuteWithToken) is permissionless by design (any relayer may front tokens) and performs NO gateway/cryptographic validation of the message. The module's _executeWithToken override only checks that a caller-SUPPLIED sourceAddress string equals the public squidRouter address — a value the caller fully controls — and never validates the real caller or a genuine Axelar gateway proof. _processPayload then decodes the target safe and delegate directly from the attacker-supplied payload and executes actions against the Safe, checking only that delegate holds permission (never msg.sender == delegate). The attacker called expressExecuteWithToken with amount = 0 (fronting nothing), the public squidRouter address string, and a forged payload naming the victim Safe, a real public NMT delegate that already held APPROVE+SWAP permission, and three actions (ERC20 approve -> Permit2 approve -> Uni V3 swap exact-in) that swap the Safe's entire USDC into a worthless attacker-controlled "u" token via the whitelisted Universal Router. This drained ~88 Safes (~$3.98M total). Root cause: missing caller/gateway authentication on the express path plus trusting payload-supplied delegate/safe. An attacker exploited New Market Trading's SquidRouterModule by forging payloads that impersonated authorized delegates, draining $3.8M from 88 Gnosis Safe wallets across Ethereum, Base, and Arbitrum in under 15 minutes. A confused-deputy vulnerability in SquidRouterModule: the contract validated the delegate via a payload field without checking that msg.sender matched the delegate, so anyone could impersonate an approved delegate and drain Safes.
